review: ISSUES:
- (miscited) "loads are governed first by drainage discharge, so export is strongly seasonal, concentrating in the non-growing season and in a few high-flow episodes \parencite{Randall2003}" — in the source Randall2003 is used only for nitrogen-timing effects (fall vs spring/nitrapyrin, 13–18% reductions), not for the hydrologic control/seasonality of nitrate export, which the source attributes to Kladivko2021, Kladivko2004, King2016, Ikenberry2014 and Speir2021.
- (miscited) "tiles frequently dominate edge-of-field phosphorus loads despite lower concentrations than surface runoff, with dissolved losses tightly coupled to soil phosphorus status and legacy phosphorus sustaining loads at watershed scale \parencite{King2015}" — in the source King2015 supports only the P-management statement (matching practice to site hydrology, connectivity, legacy P, dissolved–particulate trade-offs); the specific claims trace to Pease2018 (load dominance), Sharpley1995/Beauchemin2003 (soil-P coupling) and Jarvie2017 (legacy P at watershed scale), not King2015.
- (miscited) "cover crops---especially cereal rye, clustering around $40$--$60\%$ nitrate-load reduction \parencite{Kaspar2012}" — the source uses Kaspar2012 for a 48% concentration reduction with no significant cumulative load reduction; the 40–60% N-load-reduction clustering is attributed to Malone2018, Chatterjee2025, Malone2014b and Malone2023.
